description: Here we make a solution of the adaptive farming using nasa data
summary:
Rotation Lab is an open-source, mobile-first web app that helps farmers and agricultural extension officers adapt to shifting growing seasons by evaluating alternative crop rotations against 15+ years of historical NASA Earth data.

How It Addresses the Challenge

Addressing the Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge, Rotation Lab translates complex NASA POWER weather records (temperature extremes, precipitation, root-zone soil wetness), MODIS NDVI vegetation greenness, and NASA SMAP/IMERG satellite layers into transparent screening proxies. Utilizing standard FAO-56 dual crop coefficient modeling, the browser-based engine compares a farmer's current rotation against resilient alternatives across historical weather percentiles (P10/Median/P90). It delivers plain-language verdicts (Better, Same, Worse), what-if climate stress tests (+2°C heat, -30% rain), and an on-device AI assistant that operates offline in English, pure Hindi, and Hinglish.

Why It Is Important

Farmers are locked into traditional routines as weather patterns diverge from historical wisdom. In regions like Punjab, intensive monocultures rapidly deplete groundwater, yet growers lack accessible tools to test alternatives. By eliminating technical jargon, running client-side on mobile browsers without internet, and enforcing strict agronomic honesty, Rotation Lab empowers communities to plan resilient, water-saving crop cycles grounded in verified NASA science.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

Rotation Lab is an open-source, mobile-first decision-support platform designed for farmers, agronomists, and agricultural extension officers facing shifting climate patterns. Rather than giving opaque black-box recommendations, it acts as a screening and exploration laboratory where growers compare their current crop routines against alternative crop rotations across 15+ years of verified daily satellite and weather data.

The application follows a straightforward 3-step workflow:

  1. Locate the Farm: Users select an agro-ecological demo region (Ludhiana, Punjab in the Indo-Gangetic Plain or Ames, Iowa in the US Corn Belt), drop a pin via browser geolocation, or enter specific coordinates. An interactive map displays satellite overlays from NASA SMAP (soil moisture) and NASA IMERG (precipitation) via NASA GIBS.
  2. Describe Field & Current Crops: The grower inputs their current crop cycle (e.g., Rice in June →\rightarrow→ Wheat in November), water access mode (canal/tubewell irrigated, limited, or rainfed), and soil characteristics (using USDA texture presets like sandy loam or silt loam, or custom soil tests).
  3. Compare Alternatives Against Historical Weather: Users select up to two primary goals (e.g., Save Water, Healthy Soil, Safe in Bad Years, or More Income). The client-side engine computes supplementary irrigation requirements, soil-cover bare gaps, and climate stress across 15 historical years (2010–2024), presenting results as clear, intuitive verdicts (Better, Same, or Worse). Users can click "Why?" to inspect detailed historical percentile bands (P10 / Median / P90), agronomic trade-offs, and questions for local extension experts.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Plain-Language Agronomic Decisions: Replaces confusing composite decimals with clear verdicts (e.g., "Saves ~300 mm irrigation/year", "Fewer bare-soil days", "Better resilience to extreme heat").
  • Percentile Uncertainty Ranges (P10 / Median / P90): Instead of misleading single-number averages, rotations are evaluated across wet years, dry years, and median years, showing whether an alternative protects against downside climate risk.
  • Offline & Progressive Web App (PWA): Installs directly from the browser onto mobile devices. Demo bundles and models are cached locally so farmers can use the tool without active field cellular connectivity.
  • Complete Bilingual Equity: Native, natural Hindi (Devanagari script) and English across every screen, metric label, and printable PDF report.
  • On-Device Stress Testing: Interactive "What-If" scenario toggles replay the past 15 years under simulated +2°C warmer conditions or 30% precipitation deficits.
  • Interactive Offline AI Assistant: An on-device assistant trained to answer farm-specific questions in English, pure Hindi, and Hinglish without querying external APIs.

3. What is the intended impact?

  • Curbing Groundwater Depletion: In critical agricultural belts like Punjab, traditional rice–wheat monocultures have caused water tables to drop by 0.5–1.0 meter annually. Rotation Lab illustrates that diversified rotations (e.g., maize–soybean, sorghum–chickpea, pearl millet–lentil) can reduce irrigation requirements by 24% to 37% (saving 250–390 mm of water/year) while maintaining two cash seasons.
  • Facilitating Extension Dialogue: It bridges the gap between high-level satellite science and grassroots extension work, providing printable PDF summaries with data provenance that farmers can take to local Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) or university extension offices.
  • Building Climate-Resilient Landscapes: By highlighting unplanted bare-soil gaps, growers can identify windows for nitrogen-fixing cover crops, improving soil biological activity and erosion resistance.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, and software were used?

  • Front-End & Application Architecture: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Leaflet, React-Leaflet, and Recharts.
    • NASA POWER API: 15 years (2010–2024) of daily meteorological data (T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, T2M, PRECTOTCORR, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, and GWETROOT root-zone soil wetness) plus 45-year long-term summaries (1981–2025).
    • NASA GIBS: Real-time WMTS map tile overlays for SMAP soil moisture and IMERG precipitation.
    • ORNL DAAC / MODIS REST API: MOD13Q1 250m 16-day NDVI vegetation greenness (2019–2024) used as a ground-truth check for bare soil.
    • SoilGrids (ISRIC): Global soil baseline reference parameters.
  • Machine Learning & Python Stack: Python 3.10+, Scikit-Learn, NumPy. Trained a lightweight satellite crop classifier (78% held-out accuracy vs. 56% baseline on Iowa CDL labels) and an offline text-classification assistant (70.1% accuracy vs. 34.7% keyword baseline), compiled down to compact client-side JSON weights.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Translating Satellites into Plain Language: Rather than expecting farmers to interpret multi-spectral NDVI curves or raw millimeters of evapotranspiration, Rotation Lab automatically translates satellite and meteorological data into conversational agronomic outcomes.
  • Honest Negative-Result Science: In our ML experiments, a season greenness prediction model failed to beat the baseline on held-out test splits. Rather than keeping a flawed model, we transparently removed it from user-facing screens and published the findings in our open MODEL_CARD.md.
  • Zero-Cloud Client Architecture: All FAO-56 dual crop coefficient calculations, soil water balance evaluations, and ML assistant queries run directly inside the user's browser thread, guaranteeing total privacy, near-instant UI reactivity, and zero backend operational overhead.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Strict Agronomic Honesty: The app never claims to "forecast" future crop yields, guarantee commodity market profits, or prescribe precise irrigation amounts. It explicitly frames outputs as screening proxies derived from historical satellite weather to guide informed local discussions.
  • Accessibility & Connectivity Realities: Recognizing that agricultural fields often have poor cellular connectivity, we prioritized small bundle sizes, PWA offline caching, and desktop-to-mobile responsive layouts.
  • Cultural & Linguistic Context: Agricultural Hindi translations were developed using authentic ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research) and state extension terminology rather than mechanical machine translations, ensuring natural comprehension across different crop names, soil classes, and seasonal cycles.
